1 Introduction

oeis.tools is an R package to query the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS) from R code. It is the R counterpart of the Python oeis-tools project, and version 0.3.1 is now available on CRAN, so it no longer has to be installed from GitHub.

👉 https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=oeis.tools

2 Installation

Requires R ≥ 4.1.0.

install.packages("oeis.tools")
library(oeis.tools)

3 Examples

3.1 Reading a sequence

Sequence() downloads the OEIS entry of a sequence and exposes its fields (name, keywords, formulas, programs, cross-references…):

fib <- Sequence("A000045")

fib$name
#> [1] "Fibonacci numbers: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1."

fib$keyword
#> [1] "nonn"    "core"    "nice"    "easy"    "hear"    "changed"

3.2 Cross-references and citations

get_xref_ids() returns the A-numbers cited in the %Y lines of the entry, and get_bibtex() builds a BibTeX record ready to paste into a paper:

head(get_xref_ids(fib))
#> [1] "A001622" "A039834" "A001519" "A001906" "A001690" "A000213"

cat(get_bibtex(fib))
#> @misc{A000045,
#>   author       = {N. J. A. Sloane},
#>   title        = {A000045: Fibonacci numbers: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1.},
#>   howpublished = {The {O}n-{L}ine {E}ncyclopedia of {I}nteger {S}equences},
#>   year         = {1991},
#>   ...
#>   url          = {https://oeis.org/A000045}
#> }

3.3 Downloading and plotting b-files

BFile() downloads the b-file of a sequence (the long list of terms), and plot_data() draws it with ggplot2. With return_plot = TRUE it returns the plot object, so it can be themed and saved like any other ggplot:

library(ggplot2)

psi <- BFile("A001615")

p <- plot_data(psi, n = 1000, plot_style = "scatter",
              show = FALSE, return_plot = TRUE,
              color = "#1f6fb2", size = 0.8) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

ggsave("dedekind-psi-A001615.png", p, width = 7, height = 4.2, dpi = 150, bg = "white")

The points fall on rays through the origin: the lowest one, \(\psi(p) = p + 1\), is made of the primes, and the steeper rays collect the numbers that share the same set of small prime factors.

4 Arbitrary precision

Terms are stored as gmp::bigz integers, so sequences whose values grow beyond \(2^{53}\), the largest range where a double represents every integer exactly, keep all their digits:

head(get_bfile_data(psi))
#> Big Integer ('bigz') object of length 6:
#> [1] 1  3  4  6  6  12

When the terms are too large to convert to numbers, plot_data() switches to a \(\operatorname{sign}(a_n)\log_{10}|a_n|\) scale automatically.

5 Main functions

Function Purpose
Sequence() Download an OEIS entry and its fields
BFile() Download the b-file (terms) of a sequence
get_xref_ids() A-numbers cross-referenced by a sequence
get_bibtex() BibTeX citation of a sequence
plot_data() Plot the terms of a b-file with ggplot2

6 License

The package is distributed under the MIT License. OEIS content is available under the OEIS End-User License Agreement (CC BY-SA 4.0).

## Introduction

`oeis.tools` is an R package to query the
[On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences](https://oeis.org) (OEIS) from R
code. It is the R counterpart of the Python
[`oeis-tools`](https://github.com/oeistools/oeis-tools) project, and version **0.3.1** is
now available on **CRAN**, so it no longer has to be installed from GitHub.

👉 https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=oeis.tools

---

## Installation

Requires **R ≥ 4.1.0**.

```r
install.packages("oeis.tools")
library(oeis.tools)
```

---

## Examples

### Reading a sequence

`Sequence()` downloads the OEIS entry of a sequence and exposes its fields
(name, keywords, formulas, programs, cross-references…):

```r
fib <- Sequence("A000045")

fib$name
#> [1] "Fibonacci numbers: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1."

fib$keyword
#> [1] "nonn"    "core"    "nice"    "easy"    "hear"    "changed"
```

### Cross-references and citations

`get_xref_ids()` returns the A-numbers cited in the `%Y` lines of the entry,
and `get_bibtex()` builds a BibTeX record ready to paste into a paper:

```r
head(get_xref_ids(fib))
#> [1] "A001622" "A039834" "A001519" "A001906" "A001690" "A000213"

cat(get_bibtex(fib))
#> @misc{A000045,
#>   author       = {N. J. A. Sloane},
#>   title        = {A000045: Fibonacci numbers: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1.},
#>   howpublished = {The {O}n-{L}ine {E}ncyclopedia of {I}nteger {S}equences},
#>   year         = {1991},
#>   ...
#>   url          = {https://oeis.org/A000045}
#> }
```

### Downloading and plotting b-files

`BFile()` downloads the b-file of a sequence (the long list of terms), and
`plot_data()` draws it with `ggplot2`. With `return_plot = TRUE` it returns the
plot object, so it can be themed and saved like any other `ggplot`:

```r
library(ggplot2)

psi <- BFile("A001615")

p <- plot_data(psi, n = 1000, plot_style = "scatter",
              show = FALSE, return_plot = TRUE,
              color = "#1f6fb2", size = 0.8) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

ggsave("dedekind-psi-A001615.png", p, width = 7, height = 4.2, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
```

![Dedekind psi function $\psi(n) = n \prod_{p \mid n} (1 + 1/p)$ (A001615) for $n \le 1000$, plotted with `plot_data()`](dedekind-psi-A001615.png){fig-alt="Scatter plot of the Dedekind psi function for n up to 1000: points fan out in straight rays from the origin, the lowest ray psi(n) = n + 1 formed by the primes" fig-align="center"}

The points fall on rays through the origin: the lowest one, $\psi(p) = p + 1$,
is made of the primes, and the steeper rays collect the numbers that share the
same set of small prime factors.

## Arbitrary precision

Terms are stored as `gmp::bigz` integers, so sequences whose values grow
beyond $2^{53}$, the largest range where a `double` represents every integer
exactly, keep all their digits:

```r
head(get_bfile_data(psi))
#> Big Integer ('bigz') object of length 6:
#> [1] 1  3  4  6  6  12
```

When the terms are too large to convert to numbers, `plot_data()` switches to
a $\operatorname{sign}(a_n)\log_{10}|a_n|$ scale automatically.
